title: I Posted the Surplus-Store Coupon Photo After They Peeled the Sticker

parts.text: I carried a $12 bin to the register with an orange 50% sticker. The cashier peeled it and rang $12. The surplus policy on the pole said: STICKER PRICE STANDS. DO NOT PEEL. I was forty-three, Saturday scavenger, holding the sticky side still attached to the cashier's finger. Clerk Wes said, "Orange was a mistake." I pointed at the pole. He shrugged. "Mistakes peel." I photographed the finger, the pole, and the bin. Then I posted the still on the store's own review QR they taped to the pole. At 3:22 the manager asked why Wes's name was on a sticker-peel ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The manager can see orange residue on a finger against the do-not-peel pole.

social.video_title: The cashier peeled the 50% surplus sticker — Part 1/2
social.description: Orange bin, a sticky finger, and a pole policy. I posted the review QR. Would you have paid twelve?

parts.text: Wes called it a glitch until the camera showed the peel. I printed the ticket, the pole, and the photo. I paid $6. Wes told the back room the pole was always about optics. Optics is a word cashiers use when residue exists. Price policy now has a second line: MISTAKES DO NOT PEEL. I keep the bin. Wes leaves orange. The register finally reads the sticker.

social.video_title: Mistakes do not peel a sticker — Part 2/2
social.description: Peel ticket, six dollars, and a second line on the pole. Was a glitch ever a finger?
